# Modeling Meaning as Code — The Reference Manual

> **The book this wants to be.** Kernighan & Ritchie did not just list C's keywords; they
> taught the *idioms* — "here is the shape of problem you will meet, here is how you say it in
> this language." No such book exists for **modeling meaning**. The relational world has Codd
> and the normal forms; the warehouse world has Kimball's dimensional catalogue; the
> semantic-web world has RDF/OWL. Each is a mature pattern language for *one* target. None is a
> pattern language for capturing meaning **once**, tool-neutrally, readable by a person, a
> machine, and an AI agent alike. This manual is the attempt.

**How to read this index, and why it looks like this.** Every row below is read from the file
it names. The `status:` column is that page's OWN frontmatter, quoted — not a judgement made
here, so a page that calls itself a prototype is listed as a prototype. The counts are read
from the declarations the gates already read: `mac.schema.json`, `mac_vocabulary.yaml`, and the
runtime's implemented-canon set. Nothing on this page is typed by a person, because the
hand-written index it replaces carried three different numbers for one canon count and omitted
nine of its own pages. Pages appear in filename order within each group: no reading order is
asserted that a file does not declare. This file is `README.md` and is not listed among them.

## Findings, and how this manual is written

[`FINDINGS.md`](FINDINGS.md) records the candidate framework changes a pattern surfaced but did not enact, for the maintainer's decision. It carries **2**:

* F1 — A first-class polymorphic edge / abstract role target
* F2 — A first-class bitemporal (dual-as-of) collapse

[`AUTHORING.md`](AUTHORING.md) is the manual's authoring constitution — the rules the manual
holds itself to, including the one this index exists to satisfy: publish coverage, never a
completeness claim. A reference manual for frameworks needs its own framework.

## What holds this index

`python3 tools/gen_manual_index.py` writes this page. `python3 tools/check_manual_index.py` —
which `tools/run_framework_gates.sh` runs, because the suite globs `check_*.py` — rejects it on
four separate grounds: the index is **missing**; the index is **stale** against a fresh render;
a page **exists on disk and this index does not link it**; a page of the `keys/` subtree is
**not reachable** through the sub-index this page delegates to. The last two are asserted from a
filesystem walk against the link targets parsed out of this page as written, not from the
renderer's own model — so a renderer that silently drops a row is caught by evidence that
cannot agree with it.
